q: Which of the following is an example of error analysis in a programming class?
options: Examining students' wrong programs to find recurring misconceptions
exp: Error analysis reveals the pattern of mistakes and their causes.

q: In an experimental study, the variable manipulated by the researcher is the:
exp: The effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable is studied.

q: The term 'digital divide' refers to:
options: a break in a computer program
a division of the school into sections
the gap between those who have access to ICT and those who do not
the difference between two software versions
exp: It describes unequal access to digital technology.

q: NEP 2020 proposes that the minimum degree qualification for teaching will be:
exp: By 2030 the 4-year integrated B.Ed. is to become the minimum qualification.

q: Emotional intelligence, an idea popularised by Daniel Goleman, is the ability to:
options: recognise and manage one's own and others' emotions
exp: It includes self-awareness, self-regulation and empathy.

q: Dry-running (tracing) a program on paper helps students to:
options: understand how values change step by step
exp: Tracing builds an accurate mental model of execution.

q: The 'Zone of Proximal Development' (ZPD) given by Vygotsky refers to the gap between:
options: what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with guidance
a learner's age and mental age
the teacher's and learner's knowledge of the subject
exp: ZPD is the range of tasks a learner can complete only with help from a more knowledgeable person.

q: According to Dewey, the first step in the problem-solving method is:
exp: Dewey's steps begin with recognising a felt difficulty, then defining it, hypothesising, testing and concluding.

q: The satellite launched in 2004 exclusively for educational services in India is:
exp: EDUSAT, launched on 20 September 2004, was dedicated to educational broadcasting.

q: Asking follow-up questions to push a student to give a complete or deeper answer is the skill of:
exp: Probing prompts students to clarify, extend or justify their responses.

q: A good lesson plan should be:
options: flexible enough to be adjusted to the class situation
copied from another teacher without change
exp: Flexibility lets the teacher respond to students' needs.

q: Which of the following is a principle of curriculum construction?
exp: A good curriculum considers the needs and interests of the learner.

q: A rubric is:
options: a scoring guide listing criteria and performance levels
exp: Rubrics make scoring of projects and essays transparent and consistent.
sub: Evaluation, formative and summative assessment, CCE

q: The mean of the scores 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 is:
Which of the following would INCREASE the reliability of a test?
options: Increasing the number of good-quality items
exp: A longer test with well-written items gives more stable scores.

q: A diagnostic test differs from an achievement test because it:
options: has many small items on specific skills to locate weak points
is conducted only at the end of the year
exp: It analyses specific skills rather than giving an overall measure.

q: The dependent variable in an experiment on the effect of a new teaching method on marks is:
exp: Marks depend on the method.

q: OER stands for:
exp: OER are freely available teaching and learning materials.

q: Which body is responsible for developing the National Curriculum Framework and model textbooks?
exp: NCERT prepares the NCF and model textbooks for schools.

q: A democratic teacher in the classroom:
options: encourages participation and respects students' opinions
exp: A democratic style promotes participation and responsibility.

q: In the teaching of CS, a practical examination along with a viva voce is useful as it:
options: tests skills and understanding that written tests cannot
exp: Hands-on tasks and oral questioning show real competence.

q: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy (2001), the highest level of the cognitive domain is:
exp: The revised order is Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create.

q: Brainstorming is a technique in which:
options: only the best idea is allowed
the teacher judges every idea at once
many ideas are generated freely without immediate criticism
answers are copied from the textbook
exp: Osborn's brainstorming defers judgement to encourage a large number of creative ideas.

q: Gyan Vani, in the Indian context, is:
options: a network of educational FM radio stations
exp: Gyan Vani broadcasts educational radio programmes through FM stations.

q: In microteaching, the number of pupils generally taken is:
exp: Small groups of about 5-10 pupils are used.

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of a lesson plan?
options: It removes the need for the teacher to know the subject
exp: A lesson plan guides the teacher but cannot replace subject knowledge.

q: Which statement correctly describes a core curriculum?
options: It is for gifted students only
It contains the subjects or experiences common to all students
It is made only by students
exp: A core curriculum is the compulsory common component.

q: A cumulative record card is maintained to:
options: give rank in the class only
record the overall progress of a student over the years
exp: It stores academic, personal and social information of the student.
sub: Evaluation, formative and summative assessment, CCE

q: A test that measures what a student has learnt after instruction in a subject is called:
exp: Achievement tests measure acquired knowledge and skills.

q: Which of the following lowers the reliability of a test?
exp: Ambiguity leads to inconsistent interpretation and responses.

q: An underachiever is a student who:
options: performs below the level expected from his or her ability
exp: Underachievement is a gap between potential and performance.

q: A sample should be:
exp: Representativeness allows generalisation to the population.

q: Learners and teacher interact at the same time in:
exp: A live virtual class is a synchronous mode.

q: The role of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) is to:
options: regulate and maintain standards of teacher education
exp: NCTE recognises teacher education institutions and sets norms.

q: The 'Pygmalion effect' in classrooms means that:
options: high teacher expectations tend to raise student performance
exp: Rosenthal and Jacobson showed expectations influence achievement.

q: Explaining a stack using a pile of plates is an example of using:
exp: An analogy relates an unfamiliar concept to a familiar one.

q: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which need must be satisfied first for a child to be ready to learn?
options: Physiological needs such as food and rest
exp: Lower-level needs like hunger and sleep take priority before higher needs can motivate learning.

q: Which of the following methods is MOST teacher-centred?
exp: In the lecture method the teacher does most of the talking and decides everything.
